subject: Physics
name: Units and Measurements
cbse: Focuses on SI units, dimensions of physical quantities, dimensional analysis and its applications, errors in measurement, and significant figures.
main: Highly scoring. Focus heavily on the principles of experimental apparatus—Vernier Callipers and Screw Gauge (including zero error calculations). You must practice complex error propagation equations (e.g., fractional errors in multi-variable equations like $Z = \frac{A^2B^{1/3}}{C^3D^2}$).
advanced: Problems often combine dimensional analysis with advanced physics principles (e.g., finding the dimensions of permittivity ε₀ or permeability μ₀ using equations you won't learn until Class 12).

subject: Physics
name: Motion in a Straight Line
cbse: Elementary concepts of differentiation and integration for describing motion, uniform/non-uniform motion, and average/instantaneous velocity and acceleration.
main: Interpreting complex graphs (converting an a-t graph to a v-t or s-t graph) and handling non-uniform acceleration problems where acceleration is given as a function of velocity a(v) or position a(x) rather than time.
advanced: Multi-body problems involving relative deceleration or chasing scenarios under constraints.

subject: Physics
name: Motion in a Plane
cbse: Scalar and vector quantities, position and displacement vectors, general vectors and their notations, addition/subtraction of vectors, unit vectors, resolution of a vector, scalar and vector products. Cases of uniform velocity and uniform acceleration-projectile motion and uniform circular motion.
main: Standard projectile motion on an inclined plane (both up and down the incline). Core relative velocity problems like river-swimmer problems (minimum drift, minimum time) and rain-umbrella scenarios.
advanced: Relative motion in 2D/3D involving accelerating frames. Projectile motion where the target is also moving, or where air resistance is considered as a linear function of velocity.

subject: Physics
name: Laws of Motion
cbse: Intuitive concept of force, Inertia, Newton's laws of motion, momentum, impulse. Law of conservation of linear momentum and its applications. Equilibrium of concurrent forces, Static and kinetic friction, laws of friction, rolling friction, lubrication. Dynamics of uniform circular motion: Centripetal force, examples of circular motion (vehicle on a level circular road, vehicle on a banked road).
main: Constraint relations (string-pulley systems, wedge-block constraints). Pseudo-forces applied in accelerating frames, and multi-block systems placed on surfaces with differing coefficients of friction.
advanced: Variable mass systems (like rocket propulsion or a leaking cart, which are touched upon lightly in CBSE but mathematically rigorous in Advanced). Friction problems involving two-block and three-block systems where you must determine if the blocks move together or slide relative to each other.

subject: Physics
name: Work, Energy and Power
cbse: Work done by a constant force and a variable force; kinetic energy, work-energy theorem, power. Notion of potential energy, potential energy of a spring, conservative forces, non-conservative forces, motion in a vertical circle, elastic and inelastic collisions in one and two dimensions.
main: Calculation of work done by variable forces using definitive integration $\int F \cdot dx$. Analyzing Potential Energy Curves (U vs x) to identify points of stable, unstable, and neutral equilibrium ($F = -\frac{dU}{dx}$).
advanced: Oblique (2D) collisions where bodies have structural geometry (combining collision with rotational effects later on). Solving multi-stage tracking problems using solely the Work-Energy Theorem when multiple forces (like spring, friction, and gravity) act simultaneously.

subject: Physics
name: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
cbse: Centre of mass of a two-particle system, momentum conservation and centre of mass motion. Centre of mass of a rigid body; centre of mass of a uniform rod. Moment of a force, torque, angular momentum, conservation of angular momentum with some applications. Equilibrium of rigid bodies, rigid body rotation and equations of rotational motion, comparison of linear and rotational motions. Moment of inertia, radius of gyration, values of moments of inertia for simple geometrical objects (parallel and perpendicular axes theorems statement and applications).
main: Finding the Center of Mass of bodies with cavities (removals). Calculating the Moment of Inertia for non-uniform mass distribution using integration. Pure rolling on flat and inclined surfaces.
advanced: Highest priority chapter. Instantaneous Centre of Rotation (ICOR), Torque equations about an accelerating axis, Rolling with sliding (unveiling the transition phase), and complex conservation of angular momentum during eccentric collisions (e.g., a ball hitting a pivoting rod).

subject: Physics
name: Gravitation
cbse: Kepler's laws of planetary motion, universal law of gravitation. Acceleration due to gravity and its variation with altitude and depth. Gravitational potential energy and gravitational potential. Escape speed, orbital velocity of a satellite.
main: Calculation of gravitational fields and potentials for spherical shells and solid spheres (both inside and outside). Energy mapping of satellites in elliptical orbits.
advanced: Double star/binary star systems rotating around their common center of mass. Interplanetary trajectories, mapping gravity field variations if a tunnel is dug through the Earth.

subject: Physics
name: Mechanical Properties of Solids
cbse: Elastic behavior, Stress-strain relationship, Hooke's law, Young's modulus, bulk modulus, shear modulus of rigidity, Poisson's ratio; elastic energy.
main: Elongation of a heavy rod due to its own weight, structural thermal stress, and calculation of elastic potential energy density.
advanced: Interlinked mechanics problems where an elastic wire is subjected to rotational forces (centrifugal stretching) or dynamic loads causing oscillations.

subject: Physics
name: Mechanical Properties of Fluids
cbse: Pressure due to a fluid column; Pascal's law and its applications. Viscosity, Stokes' law, terminal velocity, streamline and turbulent flow, critical velocity, Bernoulli's theorem and its simple applications. Surface energy and surface tension, angle of contact, excess of pressure across a curved surface, application of surface tension ideas to drops, bubbles and capillary rise.
main: Speed of efflux via Venturimeter and Torricelli’s Law with non-trivial configurations. Barometer calculations when accelerated.
advanced: Fluid dynamics in accelerating or rotating containers (finding the parabolic profile of the liquid surface). Time-dependent calculations for a container emptying through a small hole. Interaction forces between two plates separated by a thin liquid film.

subject: Physics
name: Thermal Properties of Matter
cbse: Heat, temperature, thermal expansion; thermal expansion of solids, liquids and gases, anomalous expansion of water; specific heat capacity; calorimetry; change of state, latent heat capacity. Heat transfer-conduction, convection and radiation, thermal conductivity, qualitative ideas of Blackbody radiation, Wein's displacement Law, Stefan's law.
main: Calorimetry problems involving the mixing of multiple substances at different phases (ice-water-steam mixture balances). Principle of Thermal Resistance in parallel and series rod configurations.
advanced: Newton's Law of Cooling solved via exact differential equations rather than average approximations. Combination of thermal expansion with mechanical constraints (e.g., a composite rod clamped tightly between two unyielding walls).

subject: Physics
name: Thermodynamics
cbse: Thermal equilibrium and definition of temperature (zeroth law of thermodynamics). Heat, work and internal energy. First law of thermodynamics, second law of thermodynamics: gaseous state processes.
main: Calculating efficiency for arbitrary cyclic processes plotted on P-V, V-T, or P-T indicators. Reversible and irreversible processes, Carnot engine calculations.
advanced: Calculating Molar Heat Capacity (C) for a custom, non-standard polytropic process ($PV^x = \text{constant}$). Deep analysis of free expansion and entropy indications (qualitative).

subject: Physics
name: Kinetic Theory
cbse: Equation of state of an ideal gas, work done in compressing a gas. Kinetic theory of gases - assumptions, concept of pressure. Kinetic interpretation of temperature; rms speed of gas molecules; degrees of freedom, law of equi-partition of energy and application to specific heat capacities of gases; concept of mean free path.
main: Mixtures of non-reacting ideal gases (finding effective molecular mass, effective specific heat $C_v$ and $C_p$, and effective γ).
advanced: Derivations of pressure equations from basic momentum variations, and tracking gas parameter changes when molecular distributions switch or walls move dynamically.

subject: Physics
name: Oscillations
cbse: Periodic motion - time period, frequency, displacement as a function of time. Periodic functions. Simple harmonic motion (SHM) and its equation; phase; oscillations of a loaded spring-restoring force and force constant; energy in SHM - kinetic and potential energies; simple pendulum derivation of expression for its time period. Free, forced and damped oscillations, resonance.
main: Phasor Diagrams for solving the superposition of two or more SHMs and computing the minimum time taken to move between two coordinates. Combination of springs (series, parallel, and cutting of springs).
advanced: SHM of complex rigid systems (Torsional and Physical Pendulums) requiring torque evaluations (τ = -Iα). Liquid column oscillations in U-tubes, floating cylinders, or rolling cylinders tracking SHM.

subject: Physics
name: Waves
cbse: Wave motion. Longitudinal and transverse waves, speed of travelling wave, displacement relation for a progressive wave, principle of superposition of waves, reflection of waves, standing waves in strings and organ pipes, fundamental mode and harmonics, Beats.
main: Speed of a transverse wave in a hanging heavy string (where tension varies with height). Mathematical equations for Beats and the Doppler Effect in Sound (including moving source, moving observer, and reflections from walls/moving targets).
advanced: Wave intensity and power calculations. Phase changes upon reflection at a denser vs. rarer boundary. Sound wave interventions in specialized setups like Quincke's Tube.

subject: Physics
name: Electric Charges and Fields
cbse: Coulomb’s Law, electric field intensity due to a point charge, electric dipole, electric flux, Gauss’s Theorem and its simple applications (infinitely long straight wire, uniformly charged infinite plane sheet).
main: Calculation of electric fields for non-standard continuous charge distributions (e.g., rings, discs, and finite rods) using integration. Finding stable/unstable equilibrium points for a system of floating charges.
advanced: Electric field calculations for non-uniform volume charge densities (ρ as a function of r). Advanced Gauss’s Law problems involving overlapping charged spheres (cavity problems).

subject: Physics
name: Electrostatic Potential and Capacitance
cbse: Equipotential surfaces, electrical potential energy of a system of charges. Capacitors and capacitance, combination of capacitors in series and parallel, capacitance of a parallel plate capacitor with and without dielectric medium, energy stored in a capacitor.
main: Dielectric insertion/removal problems (tracking variations in Charge, Potential, and Energy when the battery remains connected vs. disconnected). Calculating equivalent capacitance for complex infinite ladder networks or asymmetric bridges using delta-star transformations.
advanced: Earthing of concentric conducting shells (charge redistribution). Self-energy of a uniformly charged solid sphere. Force between the plates of a capacitor during variable dielectric insertion.

subject: Physics
name: Current Electricity
cbse: Ohm's law, electrical resistance, V-I characteristics, drift velocity, mobility and their relation with electric current. Temperature dependence of resistance. Internal resistance of a cell, potential difference and emf of a cell, combination of cells in series and parallel. Kirchhoff's laws and simple applications. Wheatstone bridge.
main: Circuit reduction techniques (Symmetry arguments, Nodal analysis). Finding the maximum power transferred to a load (Maximum Power Transfer Theorem).
advanced: RC Circuits (Transient state analysis tracking charge charging/discharging as a function of time using differential equations $q = q_0(1 - e^{-t/\tau})$). Thermal dissipation and heating in complex networks.

subject: Physics
name: Moving Charges and Magnetism
cbse: Concept of magnetic field, Biot-Savart law and its application to a current-carrying circular loop. Ampere's law and its applications to an infinitely long straight wire and a solenoid. Force on a moving charge in uniform magnetic and electric fields. Force on a current-carrying conductor in a uniform magnetic field, force between two parallel current-carrying conductors. Torque experienced by a current loop; Moving Coil Galvanometer.
main: Motion of a charged particle in helical paths under oblique electric and magnetic fields. Conversion of a galvanometer into an ammeter/voltmeter with precise multi-range calculations.
advanced: Magnetic force on a flexible wire (calculating tension in loop shapes). Ampere's Law in cylinders with non-uniform current densities. Cycloid motion of a charge when $\vec{E}$ and $\vec{B}$ are perpendicular.

subject: Physics
name: Magnetism and Matter
cbse: Current loop as a magnetic dipole and its magnetic dipole moment, magnetic field intensity due to a magnetic dipole along its axis and perpendicular to its axis, torque on a magnetic dipole in a uniform magnetic field. Para-, dia- and ferro-magnetic substances.
main: Time period of a magnetic dipole oscillating in a magnetic field ($T = 2\pi\sqrt{I/MB}$). Properties of magnetic materials (coercivity, retentivity graphs).
advanced: Earth's magnetism calculations (True dip vs Apparent dip in different vertical planes).

subject: Physics
name: Electromagnetic Induction (EMI)
cbse: Electromagnetic induction; Faraday's laws, induced EMF and current; Lenz's Law, Eddy currents. Self and mutual induction.
main: Motional EMF (e = Bvl) in rotating rods or loops moving out of non-uniform fields. Growth and decay of current in LR Circuits.
advanced: Induced Electric Fields (Non-conservative electric fields $\oint \vec{E} \cdot \vec{dl} = -\frac{d\Phi}{dt}$). LC Oscillations (solving charge and current as harmonic equations). Interlinked mechanics-EMI problems (e.g., a rod sliding down an inclined plane under gravity inside a magnetic field with a capacitor/inductor attached).

subject: Physics
name: Alternating Current (AC)
cbse: Peak and RMS value of alternating current/voltage; reactance and impedance; LCR series circuit, resonance, power in AC circuits, wattless current. AC generator and transformer.
main: Drawing precise Phasor Diagrams to calculate phase differences. Quality factor (Q-factor) and bandwidth equations in resonant circuits.
advanced: Parallel LCR circuits and multi-loop AC networks analyzed using vector addition of admittances/impedances.

subject: Physics
name: Electromagnetic Waves
cbse: Basic idea of displacement current, Electromagnetic waves, their characteristics, their transverse nature. Electromagnetic spectrum.
main: Direct formula application linking E₀ and B₀ (c = E₀/B₀), and writing the mathematical wave equations for electric and magnetic fields in vector notation.
advanced: Calculation of Radiation Pressure and momentum imparted by an EM wave on reflecting vs. absorbing surfaces.

subject: Physics
name: Ray Optics and Optical Instruments
cbse: Reflection of light, spherical mirrors, mirror formula, refraction of light, total internal reflection and its applications, optical fibers, refraction at spherical surfaces, lenses, thin lens formula, lensmaker's formula, magnification, power of a lens, combination of thin lenses in contact, refraction of light through a prism. Optical instruments (microscopes and astronomical telescopes).
main: Apparent depth variations with moving objects/mirrors. Displacement method to find focal lengths. Minimum deviation and grazing emergence in prisms.
advanced: Vector form of Snell’s Law and Reflection. Refraction through media with a variable refractive index (n as a function of y or x) leading to curved light paths. Silvering of lenses.

subject: Physics
name: Wave Optics
cbse: Wavefront and Huygens’ principle, reflection and refraction of plane wave at a plane surface using wave fronts. Proof of laws of reflection and refraction using Huygens’ principle. Interference, Young's double slit experiment (YDSE) and expression for fringe width, coherent sources and sustained interference of light. Diffraction due to a single slit, width of central maximum.
main: YDSE with a thin transparent glass slab introduced in front of one slit. Missing wavelengths in front of one of the slits.
advanced: YDSE with non-monochromatic light (white light). Angular YDSE and YDSE placed in liquid media. Lloyd's Mirror and Thin Film Interference.

subject: Physics
name: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
cbse: Photoelectric effect, Hertz and Lenard's observations; Einstein's photoelectric equation-particle nature of light. Experimental study of photoelectric effect. Matter waves-wave nature of particles, de-Broglie relation.
main: Graph interpretations (Stopping potential vs Frequency). De-Broglie wavelength of charged particles accelerated through a potential difference V.
advanced: Photon threshold mechanics, calculating radiation pressure on skewed surfaces, and conservation of momentum during photon emission/absorption.

subject: Physics
name: Atoms
cbse: Alpha-particle scattering experiment; Rutherford's model of atom; Bohr model, energy levels, hydrogen spectrum.
main: Calculation of wave numbers using the Rydberg formula. Transitions involving Muonic atoms or highly ionized species (He⁺, Li²⁺).
advanced: Atomic Recoil (accounting for momentum conservation when an atom drops to a lower energy state and shoots out a photon). Quantization principles applied to custom hypothetical models (e.g., potential energy $U \propto r^4$).

subject: Physics
name: Nuclei
cbse: Composition and size of nucleus, Mass-energy relation, mass defect; binding energy per nucleon and its variation with mass number; nuclear fission, nuclear fusion.
main: Note: Radioactivity (Alpha, Beta, Gamma decay, and Radioactive decay law $N = N_0e^{-\lambda t}$) has been removed from CBSE but remains extremely important for both JEE Main and Advanced. Be prepared for parallel decay processes and radioactive equilibrium configurations.

subject: Physics
name: Semiconductor Electronics: Materials, Devices and Simple Circuits
cbse: Energy bands in conductors, semiconductors and insulators. p-n junction, semiconductor diode: I-V characteristics in forward and reverse bias, diode as a rectifier.
main: Note: Zener Diodes (as voltage regulators) and Logic Gates (AND, OR, NOT, NAND, NOR, XOR) are explicitly deleted from the CBSE curriculum but are guaranteed questions in almost every JEE Main session.
advanced: Advanced logic circuit analysis and ideal vs non-ideal diode mesh problems.

subject: Chemistry
name: Some Basic Concepts of Chemistry (Mole Concept)
cbse: Laws of chemical combination, atomic and molecular masses, mole concept, empirical and molecular formulas, stoichiometry, and basic concentration terms (Molarity, Molality, Mole Fraction).
main: Advanced concentration terms (Normality, % w/w, % w/v, ppm) and their interconversions. Extensive practice on Limiting Reagent problems and Sequential Reactions (where a product of one reaction becomes a reactant in the next).
advanced: Redox Titrations (Iodometry, Iodimetry, Permanganate titrations) and Eudiometry (gas analysis via volume contraction). Calculating the n-factor for complex disproportionation reactions.

subject: Chemistry
name: Structure of Atom
cbse: Bohr’s model of the hydrogen atom, dual nature of matter and light (de Broglie and Heisenberg), quantum numbers, Aufbau principle, Pauli’s exclusion principle, and Hund’s rule.
main: Calculating the wavelengths of spectral lines in the Hydrogen spectrum (Rydberg formula), counting total nodes (radial and angular), and finding the magnetic moment ($\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)}$) of ions.
advanced: Deep mathematical understanding of Schrodinger’s Wave Equation. Interpreting plots of Radial Probability Distribution Curves (R² vs r or 4π r²R² vs r). Quantum mechanics applied to multi-electron systems.

subject: Chemistry
name: Chemical Thermodynamics
cbse: Concepts of system and surroundings, state functions, first law of thermodynamics (internal energy, enthalpy, heat capacity), Hess’s law, Born-Haber cycle, entropy, and Gibbs free energy.
main: Calculating work done (W), heat (Q), Δ U, and Δ H for different thermodynamic processes (Isothermal, Adiabatic, Isobaric, Isochoric) for ideal gases.
advanced: Reversible vs. Irreversible Adiabatic processes (using $PV^\gamma = C$ vs. external pressure equations). Reversible expansion of real gases (van der Waals equations). Understanding the statistical approach to Entropy and the Third Law.

subject: Chemistry
name: Equilibrium
cbse: Law of mass action, dynamic nature of equilibrium, Le Chatelier’s principle. Ionic equilibrium: ionization of acids and bases, pH scale, salt hydrolysis (qualitative), and solubility product.
main: Finding equilibrium concentrations using $K_p$ and $K_c$. Quantitative calculations for Buffer Solutions (Henderson-Hasselbalch equation), Salt Hydrolysis (finding pH, degree of hydrolysis h), and Simultaneous Equilibrium.
advanced: Highest priority chapter. Complex solubility problems involving Simultaneous Solubility or solubility in the presence of a complexing agent. Polyprotic acid titration curves and calculating the pH of amphiprotic salts (like NaHCO₃).

subject: Chemistry
name: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
cbse: Modern periodic law, periodic table structure, trends in physical and chemical properties (atomic/ionic radii, ionization enthalpy, electron gain enthalpy, electronegativity, valence).
main: Exceptional trends (e.g., Electron gain enthalpy of Cl > F, Ionization energy of N > O). Elements with atomic numbers >100.
advanced: Inert pair effect, diagonal relationships, and screening constant calculations using Slater’s Rules. Trends across complex oxoacids and transition metal behaviors.

subject: Chemistry
name: (Part 2): Chemical Bonding and Molecular Structure
cbse: Valence electrons, ionic and covalent bonds, Lewis structures, VSEPR theory, hybridization (up to sp³d²), and Molecular Orbital Theory (MOT) for homonuclear diatomic molecules up to N₂ and O₂.
main: Predicting exact geometries and shapes including lone pair distortions. Dipole moments of organic isomers (cis vs trans, ortho/meta/para). Identifying the number of σ and π bonds in complex structures.
advanced: Back bonding, Bridge bonding (banana bonds in B₂H₆), and Silicates (classification and structure). Extended MOT for heteronuclear diatomic molecules (like CO, NO) and fractional bond order calculations for resonant species.

subject: Chemistry
name: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques
cbse: IUPAC nomenclature of simple organic compounds, electronic displacements (inductive, electromeric, resonance, hyperconjugation), homolytic and heterolytic fission, types of organic reactions (substitution, addition, elimination).
main: Systematic IUPAC nomenclature of polyfunctional compounds, bicyclo, and spiro compounds. Stability orders of reaction intermediates (carbocations, carbanions, free radicals) using General Organic Chemistry (GOC) principles. Acidic and basic strength comparisons.
advanced: Aromaticity (Huckel's rule, non-aromatic, anti-aromatic, and quasi-aromatic systems). Quantitative estimation of elements (Dumas, Kjeldahl, Carius methods). Isomerism is a massive standalone topic here: structural, geometrical, and optical isomerism (Chirality, enantiomers, diastereomers, R/S configuration, meso compounds) must be mastered.

subject: Chemistry
name: Hydrocarbons
cbse: Alkanes, Alkenes, Alkynes, and Arenes (Benzene). IUPAC nomenclature, physical properties, chemical reactions (halogenation, addition of HX via Markovnikov's rule, ozonolysis, nitration, sulphonation, Friedel-Crafts alkylation/acylation).
main: Mechanism of free radical halogenation of alkanes. Peroxide effect (Anti-Markovnikov addition). Ozonolysis mechanism and tracking reactants from final products.
advanced: Detailed reaction mechanisms including structural rearrangements (carbocation shifts—hydride and methyl shifts). Stereochemistry of addition reactions (e.g., syn vs anti addition of bromine to cis/trans alkenes yielding racemic or meso mixtures). Electrophilic aromatic substitution mechanism with activating/deactivating directing groups.

subject: Chemistry
name: Solutions
cbse: Types of solutions, expression of concentration of solids in liquids, solubility of gases in liquids (Henry's Law), Raoult's Law, ideal and non-ideal solutions, colligative properties (relative lowering of vapor pressure, elevation of boiling point, depression of freezing point, osmotic pressure), and determination of molecular mass using colligative properties.
main: Extensive calculation involving the van 't Hoff factor (i) for solutes undergoing partial association or dissociation.
advanced: Thermodynamics of non-ideal solutions (ΔH_mix, ΔV_mix, ΔS_mix, and ΔG_mix signs). Vapor pressure mapping of ternary mixtures or immisicible liquids (steam distillation principles).

subject: Chemistry
name: Electrochemistry
cbse: Redox reactions, conductance in electrolytic solutions, specific and molar conductivity, variations of conductivity with concentration, Kohlrausch's Law, electrolysis and laws of electrolysis (Faraday's laws), EMF of a cell, standard electrode potential, Nernst equation and its application to chemical cells, and Relation between Gibbs energy change and EMF of a cell.
main: Direct application of the Nernst Equation to find unknown concentration or pH of half-cells. Calculation of equilibrium constants ($K_{eq}$) from standard potentials.
advanced: Concentration cells (with and without transference). Calculation of thermodynamic parameters (Δ H, Δ S) from the temperature coefficient of cell EMF (dE/dT). Solubility Product ($K_{sp}$) determinations using electrochemical setups.

subject: Chemistry
name: Chemical Kinetics
cbse: Rate of a reaction (average and instantaneous), factors affecting rate of reaction: concentration, temperature, catalyst; order and molecularity of a reaction, rate law and specific rate constant, integrated rate equations and half-life (only for zero and first-order reactions), concept of collision theory (elementary idea, no mathematical treatment), and Activation energy (Arrhenius equation).
main: Determining reaction orders from experimental data tables. Calculations involving pseudo-first-order reactions and monitoring kinetics via physical parameters (like pressure, volume of gas evolved, or optical rotation).
advanced: Parallel, sequential, and reversible reactions (e.g., A → B and A → C simultaneously). Deriving rate laws using the Steady-State Approximation. Multi-step mechanism analyses involving catalyst equilibria.

subject: Chemistry
name: The d- and f-Block Elements
cbse: General introduction, electronic configuration, occurrence and characteristics of transition metals, general trends in properties of the first-row transition metals (metallic character, ionization enthalpy, oxidation states, ionic radii, color, catalytic property, magnetic properties, interstitial compounds, alloy formation), and preparation and properties of K₂Cr₂O₇ and KMnO₄.
main: Exceptional configurations and oxidations states of Lanthanides and Actinides (Lanthanide contraction origins and consequences).
advanced: Deep understanding of the oxidizing mechanisms of KMnO₄ and K₂Cr₂O₇ in acidic, basic, and neutral media, including balancing complex ionic equations. Structures of chromate, dichromate, manganate, and permanganate ions.

subject: Chemistry
name: Coordination Compounds
cbse: Coordination compounds - Introduction, ligands, coordination number, color, magnetic properties and shapes, IUPAC nomenclature of mononuclear coordination compounds. Bonding (Werner's theory, VBT, and CFT). Structural and stereoisomerism.
main: Determining hybridization, inner vs. outer orbital complexes, and calculating Spin-Only Magnetic Moments. Basic IUPAC nomenclature including bridging ligands.
advanced: Highest priority inorganic chapter. High-level Stereoisomerism (counting total geometrical and optical isomers for complex formulas like $[M(aa)_2b_2]$). Quantitative calculation of Crystal Field Stabilization Energy (CFSE) for octahedral and tetrahedral geometries, tracking high-spin vs. low-spin configurations, and understanding the Jahn-Teller distortion.

subject: Chemistry
name: Haloalkanes and Haloarenes
cbse: Nomenclature, nature of C-X bond, physical and chemical properties, mechanism of substitution reactions, optical rotation.
main: Complete mastery of $S_N1, S_N2, E1, E2$ mechanisms. Stereochemical outcomes (inversion vs. racemization). Nucleophilic aromatic substitutions ($S_NAr$ and Benzyne mechanism).

subject: Chemistry
name: Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers
cbse: Nomenclature, methods of preparation, physical and chemical properties (of primary, secondary and tertiary alcohols); mechanism of dehydration, identification of primary, secondary and tertiary alcohols; mechanism of electrophilic substitution, acidic nature of phenol.
main: Pinacol-Pinacolone rearrangement, Hydroboration-Oxidation (HBO) vs. Oxymercuration-Demercuration (OMDM), Reimer-Tiemann reaction, and Kolbe’s reaction mechanisms. Cleavage of unsymmetrical ethers by HI (tracking $S_N1$ vs $S_N2$ pathways).

subject: Chemistry
name: Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids
cbse: Nomenclature, nature of carbonyl group, methods of preparation, physical and chemical properties, mechanism of nucleophilic addition, reactivity of alpha hydrogen in aldehydes.
main: The most crucial organic chapter. Thorough mechanical understanding of name reactions: Aldol Condensation (intramolecular, crossed), Cannizzaro Reaction, Clemmensen and Wolff-Kishner reductions, Haloform reaction, and HVZ reaction. Carboxylic acid derivatives reactivity orders.

subject: Chemistry
name: Amines
cbse: Nomenclature, classification, structure, methods of preparation, physical and chemical properties, uses, identification of primary, secondary and tertiary amines. Diazonium salts: Preparation, chemical reactions and importance in synthetic organic chemistry.
main: Quantitative basic strength comparison in gaseous vs. aqueous phases (steric hindrance vs. hydration effects). Hoffmann Bromamide degradation mechanism and Hoffmann Exhaustive Methylation. Coupling reactions of diazonium salts.

subject: Chemistry
name: Biomolecules
cbse: Carbohydrates, Proteins, Vitamins, Nucleic Acids.
main: Structures of Glucose, Fructose, and Sucrose (Haworth projections, mutarotation, reducing vs. non-reducing behaviors). Peptide bond formations, structures of amino acids (essential vs non-essential, Isoelectric points), and DNA/RNA nitrogenous base pairings.

subject: Mathematics
name: Sets
cbse: Sets and their representations, empty set, finite and infinite sets, subsets, power set, universal set, Venn diagrams, union and intersection of sets.
main: Understanding the properties of set operations (laws of union, intersection, and complements). Word problems involving 3-set Venn diagrams with complex constraints.

subject: Mathematics
name: Relations and Functions
cbse: Cartesian product of sets, definition of relation, domain, co-domain and range of a relation. Function as a special type of relation, domain, co-domain and range of a function. Real-valued functions, graphs of standard functions (identity, constant, linear, polynomial, rational, modulus, signum, exponential, logarithmic, greatest integer function).
main: Finding the Domain and Range of complex composite functions involving square roots, fractions, and logarithms.
advanced: Note: Classification of functions (one-to-one, onto, many-to-one, into) and composite/inverse functions are technically introduced in Class 12 CBSE but must be mastered right now for JEE. Deeply understand transformations of graphs (e.g., pulling f(x) to |f(x)| or f(|x|)).

subject: Mathematics
name: Trigonometric Functions
cbse: Radian and degree measures, definition of trigonometric functions with the help of a unit circle, signs of trigonometric functions, identities, addition/subtraction formulas, multiple and sub-multiple angle formulas, general solution of trigonometric equations (removed from modern CBSE but active in JEE).
main: Finding values of conditional trigonometric identities, solving trigonometric equations, and finding the number of principal solutions in specified intervals.
advanced: Summation of trigonometric series (using C+iS method or differences). In-depth mastery of Inverse Trigonometric Functions (graphical properties and identities, which CBSE keeps in Class 12).

subject: Mathematics
name: Complex Numbers and Quadratic Equations
cbse: Need for complex numbers, fundamental operations, conjugate, modulus, and argument of complex numbers. Linear and quadratic equations with complex roots.
main: Properties of modulus, argument, and conjugate. Roots of unity (properties of ω and ω²). For Quadratics: Condition for common roots, nature of roots, and relation between roots and coefficients.
advanced: Geometric representation of complex numbers (equations of straight lines, circles, ellipses, and regions in the Argand plane). Location of Roots in quadratic equations under strict constraints (e.g., both roots lie between k₁ and k₂). Higher-degree polynomial equations.

subject: Mathematics
name: Linear Inequalities
cbse: Linear inequalities, algebraic solutions of linear inequalities in one variable and their representation on the number line.
main: Mastery of the Wavy Curve Method (Interval method) to solve rational, algebraic, and radical inequalities. Absolute value (modulus) inequalities.

subject: Mathematics
name: Permutations and Combinations (P&C)
cbse: Fundamental principle of counting, factorial n!, Permutations as an arrangement and Combinations as a selection, derivation of formulas for $^nP_r$ and $^nC_r$ and their connections.
main: Standard word problems involving arrangements (words, numbers), restricted selections, and circular permutations. Finding the "rank of a word" in a dictionary.
advanced: Exponent of a prime p in n! (Legendre's Formula). Beggar's Method (distribution of identical objects to distinct bins using multinomial theorem), Derangements (objects not going to their specified destinations), and Inclusion-Exclusion Principle.

subject: Mathematics
name: Binomial Theorem
cbse: Historical introduction, statement and proof of the binomial theorem for positive integral indices. General and middle term.
main: Finding independent terms, specific coefficients, and fractional/integral parts of numbers. Remainder calculations using binomial expansion.
advanced: Binomial Coefficients Series (summation involving products of coefficients, using differentiation/integration techniques on expansion series). Binomial theorem for any rational index.

subject: Mathematics
name: Sequences and Series
cbse: Arithmetic Progression (AP), Geometric Progression (GP), general term, sum of n terms, arithmetic mean (AM) and geometric mean (GM).
main: Arithmetico-Geometric Progression (AGP), Telescoping series (finding the sum of a series using $T_n = V_n - V_{n-1}$), and properties of AM, GM, HM.
advanced: Advanced problems on AM-GM-HM Inequalities to find the minimum/maximum values of multi-variable expressions.

subject: Mathematics
name: Straight Lines
cbse: Slope of a line and angle between two lines. Various forms of equations of a line: parallel to axes, point-slope form, slope-intercept form, two-point form, intercept form, normal form. Distance of a point from a line.
main: Shifting of origin, Concurrency of lines, Equations of internal/external angle bisectors, and finding coordinates of Orthocentre, Circumcentre, and Incentre.
advanced: Pair of Straight Lines (homogeneous and non-homogeneous second-degree equations, angle between them, and point of intersection). Distance between parallel lines, image of a point with respect to a line, and family of straight lines (L₁ + λ L₂ = 0).

subject: Mathematics
name: Conic Sections
cbse: Sections of a cone: circles, ellipse, parabola, hyperbola. Standard equations and simple properties of a Circle, Parabola, Ellipse, and Hyperbola.
main: Standard equations of tangents and normals to all conics. Condition of tangency (c = a/m, etc.). Chord of contact, chord bisected at a given point.
advanced: The most rigorous geometry zone. Equations of normals to conics and calculating co-normal points. Common tangents between two different conics (e.g., a circle and a parabola). Properties of focal chords, Rectangular Hyperbola (xy = c²), and asymptotes.

subject: Mathematics
name: Introduction to Three-Dimensional Geometry
cbse: Coordinate axes and coordinate planes in three dimensions. Coordinates of a point. Distance between two points and section formula.
main: This acts as a soft introduction. Keep it restricted to basic distance and section formulas, as the real core of 3D geometry (Lines and Planes) is evaluated via vectors in Class 12.

subject: Mathematics
name: Limits and Derivatives
cbse: Intuitive idea of limit. Limits of polynomial and rational functions, trigonometric, exponential and logarithmic functions. Definition of derivative, derivative as a rate of change, slope of tangent line, derivatives of algebraic, trigonometric functions (using first principle and standard rules).
main: Evaluating indeterminate forms ($\frac{0}{0}, \frac{\infty}{\infty}$) using factorization, rationalization, and standard expansions. Standard L'Hôpital's Rule.
advanced: Evaluating complex limit forms ($1^\infty, 0^0, \infty^0$). Evaluation of limits using the Squeeze Theorem (Sandwich Theorem). First Principle derivatives applied to non-differentiable points.

subject: Mathematics
name: Statistics
cbse: Measures of dispersion: Range, Mean deviation, variance and standard deviation of ungrouped/grouped data.
main: High reward for low effort. Guaranteed 1 question in almost every JEE Main paper. Focus entirely on the mathematical effects on Mean, Variance, and Standard Deviation when data points are multiplied, added, or deleted.

subject: Mathematics
name: Probability
cbse: Random experiments; outcomes, sample spaces. Events; occurrence of events, 'not', 'and' and 'or' events, exhaustive events, mutually exclusive events, Axiomatic probability.
main: Note: Class 11 probability is purely theoretical. For JEE, merge this instantly with Permutations & Combinations. Master Conditional Probability, Bayes' Theorem, and Binomial Distribution (which are Class 12 CBSE topics but form the core of JEE Advanced probability questions).

subject: Mathematics
name: Relations and Functions
cbse: Types of relations (reflexive, symmetric, transitive, and equivalence relations). One-to-one (injective) and onto (surjective) functions.
main: Finding the domain and range of complex composite functions. Testing for injectivity and surjectivity using calculus techniques (derivative tests for monotonicity).
advanced: Determining the functional equations from given conditions. Number of injective/surjective mappings using Permutations & Combinations formulas. Inverse of fractional/piecewise functions.

subject: Mathematics
name: Inverse Trigonometric Functions (ITF)
cbse: Definition, range, domain, and principal value branches of ITFs. Graphs of basic trigonometric inverse functions.
main: Simplifying complex trigonometric expressions by changing variables. Solving algebraic equations involving inverse functions.
advanced: Summation of finite and infinite series involving inverse tangents ($\tan^{-1}$). Handling multi-variable equations under boundary constraints by looking at domain restrictions.

subject: Mathematics
name: Matrices
cbse: Concept, notation, order, equality, and types of matrices. Operations (addition, scalar multiplication, matrix multiplication). Symmetric and skew-symmetric matrices.
main: Properties of symmetric, skew-symmetric, orthogonal, and idempotent matrices. Finding higher powers of matrices ($A^n$) by identifying patterns.
advanced: Matrix properties combined with mathematical induction or sequences. Trace of matrices and properties of eigenvalues/characteristic equations.

subject: Mathematics
name: Determinants
cbse: Determinant of a square matrix (up to 3 × 3). Minors, cofactors, and applications in finding the area of a triangle. Adjoint and inverse of a square matrix. Solving systems of linear equations in two or three variables using matrix inverses.
main: Cramer’s Rule for solving systems of linear equations (trivial vs. non-trivial solutions, consistency checks). Direct properties of adjoints ($\vert{}\text{adj}(A)\vert{} = \vert{}A\vert{}^{n-1}$).
advanced: Evaluating complex determinants using row/column transformations and functional parameters. Differentiating a determinant whose elements are functions of x.

subject: Mathematics
name: Continuity and Differentiability
cbse: Continuity and differentiability of composite functions. Derivative of chain rule, implicit functions, inverse trigonometric functions, exponential, and logarithmic functions. Second-order derivatives.
main: Finding unknown constants by matching Left-Hand and Right-Hand Limits/Derivatives. Derivatives of functions with respect to other functions (parametric form).
advanced: Checking the differentiability of functions containing absolute values or greatest integer steps (e.g., $f(x) = [x]\sin(\pi x)$) using graphical analysis or the functional definition of derivatives.

subject: Mathematics
name: Applications of Derivatives (AOD)
cbse: Rate of change of quantities, increasing/decreasing functions, maxima, and minima (First and Second Derivative Tests).
main: Extreme values of functions on closed intervals. Approximations using differentials.
advanced: Highest priority calculus chapter. Rolle's Theorem and Lagrange's Mean Value Theorem (LMVT) applications in checking the roots of equations. Maxima/minima problems involving dynamic geometric optimization (e.g., maximizing cylinders inside cones). Concavity and point of inflection analysis (f''(x) = 0).

subject: Mathematics
name: Integrals (Indefinite & Definite)
cbse: Integration as inverse process of differentiation. Integration by substitution, partial fractions, and by parts. Fundamental Theorem of Calculus. Basic properties of definite integrals.
main: Standard integration forms involving trigonometric combinations or rational functions. Definite integration using properties like the King's Property ($\int_a^b f(x)dx = \int_a^b f(a+b-x)dx$).
advanced: Leibniz Rule for differentiating under the integral sign. Definite integral as the limit of a sum. Integration of highly discontinuous, fractional, or greatest integer functions.

subject: Mathematics
name: Applications of the Integrals (Area Under Curve)
cbse: Area under simple curves, especially lines, circles, parabolas, and ellipses (standard forms only).
main: Finding the area of regions bounded between two standard curves (e.g., a parabola and a line).
advanced: Calculating areas of bounded regions defined via inequalities (e.g., $\{(x,y) : y^2 \le 4x, 4x^2 + 4y^2 \le 9\}$) and dealing with multi-intersection layouts.

subject: Mathematics
name: Differential Equations
cbse: Order and degree, general and particular solutions of a differential equation. Separation of variables method. Homogeneous differential equations. Linear differential equations of the form $\frac{dy}{dx} + Py = Q$.
main: Direct formulation of an Integrating Factor ($\text{I.F.} = e^{\int P dx}$) to solve standard first-order linear differential equations. Word problems on population growth or cooling rates.
advanced: Exact differential forms (reducing complex expressions to d(xy), d(x/y), etc.). Orthogonal trajectories and reducing non-linear equations into linear forms using substitutions (Bernoulli's Equation).

subject: Mathematics
name: Vectors
cbse: Vectors and scalars, magnitude and direction. Direction cosines and direction ratios. Types of vectors. Dot and cross products of vectors, projection of a vector on a line.
main: Properties of cross product areas, applications of work done and torque.
advanced: Scalar Triple Product (STP) ($[\vec{a} \ \vec{b} \ \vec{c}]$) representing parallelopiped volumes, and Vector Triple Product (VTP) ($\vec{a} \times (\vec{b} \times \vec{c})$). Solving complex vector equations involving unknown vectors.

subject: Mathematics
name: Three-Dimensional Geometry (3D)
cbse: Direction cosines and direction ratios of a line joining two points. Cartesian and vector equation of a line, coplanar and skew lines, shortest distance between two lines.
main: Note: Equations of Planes have been removed from the recent CBSE syllabus but are guaranteed questions in JEE Main. Finding the shortest distance between skew lines.
advanced: Intersections of lines and planes, finding the image of a point or line with respect to a plane, and equations of a family of planes. Bisectors of angles between two planes.

subject: Mathematics
name: Probability
cbse: Conditional probability, multiplication theorem on probability, independent events, total probability, and Bayes' Theorem.
main: Direct applications of Bayes' Theorem. Calculating means and variances using the Binomial Distribution (Bernoulli trials).
advanced: Geometric probability setups. Solving problems involving infinite loops (e.g., games that keep going until someone wins) and complex game states using recursive algebraic modeling.
